✦   A Young Jedi Adventure   ✦
Lats'e
and the
Lost Younglings
🐱
Featuring Sharder the Lloth Cat
Chapter One
A Big Day

Lats'e woke up early.

The sun was just rising over the Jedi Temple. Its warm light came through her window. Lats'e stretched her arms way, way up.

Then she heard a little sound.

Mrrrow.

Her Lloth Cat, Sharder, jumped onto the bed. He was soft and round and had big green eyes. He rubbed his fuzzy head right on her chin.

"Good morning, Sharder," said Lats'e. She scratched behind his pointy ears. He purred like a little engine.

Purrrr. Purrrr. Purrrr.

Lats'e smiled. Today felt like a special day. She could feel it in the Force.

The Force is a special power that flows through all living things. Jedi can feel it, use it, and listen to it. Lats'e was still learning. But she was getting very good.

She got dressed fast. She clipped her lightsaber to her belt. She patted Sharder on the head.

"Come on," she said. "Let's go see what today brings."

Down in the great hall, Master Yoda was waiting. He smiled when he saw Lats'e coming.

"Good morning, young Lats'e," said Master Yoda. "A mission I have for you."

Lats'e stood up very straight. "A real mission?"

"Yes," said Master Yoda. "Three younglings went on a field trip to the planet Onderon. But now... lost they are. Help them, you must."

Lats'e's eyes went wide. She looked down at Sharder. Sharder looked back up at her.

"We can do it," said Lats'e. "We will find them."

Master Yoda nodded slowly. "Trust in the Force. Trust in yourself."

Lats'e gave Sharder a little squeeze. Then she ran to the hangar bay.

It was time to fly.

Chapter Two
Into the Sky

Lats'e's ship was small and fast. It was green and white, like a flying leaf. She called it the Breeze.

She climbed into the pilot's seat. Sharder jumped in beside her. He sat in the co-pilot seat like he owned it.

Lats'e laughed. "You are so silly."

Sharder blinked.

Lats'e checked all the buttons. She checked all the switches. She was a very good pilot. She had practiced a lot.

"Okay," she said. "Breeze, let's go to Onderon."

She pushed the controls. The Breeze hummed and lifted off the ground. Up, up, up it went! Then —

WHOOOOOOSH!

They jumped into hyperspace! Stars became long white lines all around them. Lats'e smiled. She loved flying more than almost anything.

In no time at all, they came back out of hyperspace. Right in front of them was Onderon — a big, round, green planet. It was covered in tall, tall trees.

"Wow," said Lats'e. "That is a lot of jungle."

Sharder meowed.

"I know," she said. "The younglings could be anywhere."

Lats'e closed her eyes. She took a slow, deep breath. She reached out with the Force. It was like a warm wave spreading out from her heart — touching every tree, every bug, every drop of water on that planet far below.

She felt the trees swaying. She felt little animals running. She felt a river rushing.

And then...

She felt something else.

Three small, scared, beating hearts.

The Force told her: They are there. In the jungle. And they need you.

Lats'e opened her eyes. "I found them!"

She pointed the Breeze toward the jungle. Down, down, down they flew — through the clouds, past the treetops — until she found a small clearing to land in.

Thunk.

They were on the ground. The adventure was about to begin.

Chapter Three
The Big Creature

The jungle of Onderon was amazing.

Tall purple trees reached up to the sky. Strange flowers glowed with soft blue light. Funny little bugs flew around in sparkly clouds.

"Whoa," said Lats'e.

Sharder sniffed the air. His tail twitched back and forth. He sniffed left. He sniffed right. Then he looked up at Lats'e as if to say: Well? Let's go!

Lats'e followed her feeling in the Force. She walked through tall green grass. She stepped over big, twisty roots. She ducked under low branches.

Then she heard it.

"Help! Help!"

She ran toward the voice.

Three younglings were hiding inside a big hollow log. They had pressed themselves all the way to the back. They had wide, frightened eyes.

One was a tiny green Rodian with long fingers. One was a tall Zabrak with little hornlets on her head. One was a fluffy little Ewok with enormous round ears.

"Hello!" said Lats'e with a kind smile. "My name is Lats'e. I am a Jedi in training. I came here to help you."

"There's a MONSTER out there!" cried the Rodian.

"It is HUGE!" said the Zabrak.

"Very scary!" said the Ewok.

Just then — CRASH! BOOM! CRASH!

Something very big was moving through the trees. The ground shook with every step. Leaves fell from the branches above.

Lats'e turned around.

Through the purple trees came the biggest creature she had ever seen. It was called a Boma Beast. It was almost as tall as two houses. Its skin was thick and gray. It had three big horns on its head and four stomping feet. Its eyes were bright, bright yellow.

The Boma Beast stopped.

It looked at Lats'e.

Lats'e looked back at it.

She did not run. She did not scream. She took a breath and looked — really looked — at the creature.

And then she saw it.

The creature's front left foot was caught in a long, thick vine. The vine had wrapped itself around and around. The more the Boma Beast had pulled, the tighter it had gotten. The creature's foot was red and sore.

The big yellow eyes were not angry. They were scared. And tired. And hurting.

"Oh," said Lats'e softly. "You are not a monster at all. You are hurt."

Sharder walked right up beside Lats'e. He sat down and stared at the creature with calm green eyes.

The Boma Beast made a very quiet sound. Almost like a question.

Chapter Four
Being Kind

Lats'e turned back to the hollow log.

"It is safe," she said gently. "Come out. I will show you something."

Slowly, slowly, the three younglings crawled out of the log. They stayed very close to Lats'e and held onto her cloak.

"But it is SO big!" said the Rodian.

"Big does not mean bad," said Lats'e. "Look at its foot. Do you see the vine?"

The younglings looked. They squinted. The Rodian gasped. "Oh! It is stuck!"

"It was not chasing you to be mean," said Lats'e. "It was walking around because it was in pain. It could not stop moving."

The Zabrak looked at the big creature's yellow eyes. The creature looked back at her. It made that quiet little sound again.

"It does look sad," said the Zabrak quietly.

"What do we do?" asked the Ewok.

"We help it," said Lats'e. "Together."

Lats'e stepped forward slowly. She held out her hand, palm open, so the Boma Beast could see she meant no harm. The creature dipped its great big head down a little.

Then Lats'e closed her eyes. She reached into the Force. She could feel the vine — thick and twisty and very, very tight. She focused hard. She pushed with the Force, gentle and steady, like a warm hand unwinding a knot.

The vine began to move. Slowly... slowly... slowly...

Snap.

The vine fell away.

The Boma Beast lifted its big foot. It set it back down. It lifted it again. No pain. It was free!

Then the creature lifted its giant head and let out a mighty sound:

ROOOOOOOOAR!

The three younglings jumped back. The Ewok grabbed Lats'e's hand. But Lats'e stood still and smiled.

Because the creature was not roaring in anger. It was roaring in joy.

The Boma Beast lowered its enormous head all the way down to the ground. It looked at Lats'e with those big yellow eyes.

And it blinked.

Slowly. Kindly. Like a thank you.

Lats'e walked forward and gently placed her hand on the creature's enormous, warm nose.

Then Sharder trotted over. He sniffed the creature's nose. The Boma Beast sniffed back. Then — bonk — Sharder bumped his little cat forehead right against the creature's giant snout.

Everyone burst out laughing.

The Rodian walked over next. She reached out her small green hand and touched the creature's cheek. "Hi," she said, very softly. "I am sorry we were scared of you."

The creature blinked again.

The Zabrak and the Ewok came over too. They each gave the Boma Beast a gentle pat.

The great creature stood up tall. It looked at them all one last time with its warm yellow eyes. Then it turned and walked slowly and happily back into the purple trees.

They watched it go until it disappeared.

The jungle was quiet.

"That was the most amazing thing I have ever seen," said the Zabrak.

"That was YOU," said Lats'e. "All of you. You were brave. And you were kind. That is what Jedi do."

The Ewok looked up at her with big eyes. "Is that what the Force is? Being kind?"

Lats'e thought about it. "Being kind is one of the best things the Force can teach us," she said. "When you are kind, good things happen. Even with scary things."

Being kind is always the right choice — even when it is hard, even when you are scared.
Chapter Five
Home

They walked back through the jungle together.

The glowing blue flowers lit up the path ahead of them. The sparkly bugs danced in little clouds. The tall purple trees waved their branches in the breeze.

The younglings told Lats'e all about how they had gotten lost. They had followed the glowing flowers deeper and deeper into the jungle. Before they knew it, they had no idea which way was the ship.

"These flowers?" asked Lats'e, pointing at the soft blue blooms along the path.

"Yes!" said the Rodian. "They are so beautiful. We just kept following them."

Lats'e smiled. She reached out with the Force — gently, like picking up something precious — and lifted three of the glowing flowers from their stems. They floated through the air, spinning slowly, glowing softly blue.

She gave one to each youngling.

Their eyes lit up even brighter than the flowers.

When they reached the Breeze, Lats'e opened the hatch. Everyone piled in. It was a little crowded. The Ewok sat in Lats'e's seat for a moment by accident. The Zabrak bumped her horns on the ceiling. The Rodian found Sharder's food bowl and accidentally knocked it over.

It was a little chaotic. It was also very fun.

Sharder climbed straight onto the Ewok's lap and began to purr. The Ewok looked like all her dreams had come true at once.

Lats'e sat in the pilot's seat. She powered up the Breeze. The engines hummed. The lights blinked on one by one.

"Is everyone ready?" she called.

"YES!" said three voices.

Up, up, up they flew. Through the leaves of the tall purple trees. Through the clouds. Through the blue sky. And then —

WHOOOOOOSH!

Into the stars.

When the Breeze landed back at the Jedi Temple, Master Yoda was standing right there on the landing pad. He leaned on his little walking stick. His big ears were raised up. He was smiling.

The three younglings ran out and all started talking at once. Their voices tumbled over each other like puppies.

"She found us with the Force—"

"And there was this GIANT creature—"

"And she freed it and it roared and it was the best thing EVER—"

"And then her CAT bonked it on the nose!"

Master Yoda listened to every word. Then he turned to look at Lats'e.

She was standing quietly. Sharder was draped over her shoulder like a fuzzy scarf, purring away.

"Proud of you, I am," said Master Yoda. "Used the Force well, you did. But more than that — your heart you used."

Lats'e felt something warm bloom in her chest. Not just from his words. But because she knew, deep in her heart, that she had done the right thing.

She had used her piloting to get there.

She had used the Force to find the younglings and free the creature.

She had used her lightsaber... not at all, actually. Because sometimes the best thing a Jedi can do is put the lightsaber away.

And she had taught the younglings — and maybe herself — something true: being kind is one of the bravest things you can ever do.

Lats'e scratched Sharder behind the ears. He purred louder.

"We make a pretty good team," she said to him.

Sharder meowed.

Above the Jedi Temple, the stars were coming out one by one. They sparkled and twinkled against the deep, dark sky.

Like they were saying: Yes. Yes, you do.

THE END

May the Force be with you — always. ✨
